article_title: MariaDB Enterprise Platform 2027 Is Generally Available; Its 56% Throughput Claim Rests on a MariaDB-Sponsored Test MariaDB Calls Non-Durable
summary: Approved after manual source verification of all five snapshots. The script's APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS came only from the mariadb.com allowlist warning; mariadb.com was independently confirmed as MariaDB plc's official site and added to config/source_allowlist.txt, and every claim, quote, number and date traced to a snapshot.

findings.message: mariadb.com allowlist warning resolved by editorial confirmation
findings.details: mariadb.com is MariaDB plc's (MariaDB Corporation Ab's) own site: the MariaDB Foundation's mariadb.org/about page links 'MariaDB Corporation' to https://mariadb.com; the mariadb-corporation GitHub organization lists https://mariadb.com as its website; MariaDB plc's SEC filings (CIK 0001929589, Redwood City, CA, the same dateline as the press release) use the XBRL namespace http://mariadb.com/20230930. Added to config/source_allowlist.txt with a justification comment; mariadb.org is the separate Foundation site. blocksandfiles.com was already allowlisted.

Title is 141 characters, under the 150-character threshold. The non-durable description is attributed to MariaDB in the title ('a MariaDB-Sponsored Test MariaDB Calls Non-Durable') and in the summary ('MariaDB's own blog calls in-memory and non-durable'); the Herald does not itself assert wrongdoing. Every element of the title traces to a snapshot (sponsorship: press release footnote 'Sponsored by MariaDB.' and report page 'sponsored by MariaDB'; non-durable: engineering blog 'The configuration was deliberately in-memory and non-durable.').

Four of five sources are MariaDB's own pages (press release, launch blog, engineering blog, gated-report landing page) and are used as primary sources for MariaDB's own statements; the article attributes each and states the McKnight report itself was not read. Blocks & Files (Chris Mellor, 4 Nov 2026) is independent of MariaDB but adds no verification: it largely repeats the press release (components, 30% vector figure, '56 percent higher peak throughput over the last major release in third-party testing', CEO quote) and omits the sponsorship and test conditions, which the article says accurately. This is a News article, so the 2-independent-source rule for Analysis does not apply. No suspicious_patterns in any manifest entry.

content_preview.title: MariaDB Enterprise Platform 2027 Is Generally Available; Its 56% Throughput Claim Rests on a MariaDB-Sponsored Test MariaDB Calls Non-Durable
content_preview.summary: MariaDB plc says Enterprise Platform 2027 is generally available. Its 56% peak-throughput claim over version 11.8 rests on a MariaDB-sponsored HammerDB test that MariaDB's own blog calls in-memory and non-durable.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

MariaDB plc announced MariaDB Enterprise Platform 2027 on November 4, 2026, and said in its [press release](https://mariadb.com/newsroom/press-releases/mariadb-launches-into-the-agentic-era-with-an-agent-ready-platform-and-a-bold-new-brand) that the platform "is generally available today." According to the same release, the platform includes MariaDB Enterprise Server 12.3, MariaDB Exa, MariaDB GridGain, MariaDB MaxScale, MariaDB Enterprise Manager and the MariaDB Enterprise Kubernet...

editor_notes.content_quality: News article of about 832 words (News range 400-1200). Structure: Overview, 'What MariaDB Says Is New', 'How the 56% Figure Was Produced', 'Availability Wording Differs', 'What We Don't Know'. Neutral, attributed throughout ('MariaDB says', 'as described by MariaDB'); no AI self-reference, no editorializing beyond the title's framing, which is attributed to MariaDB's own wording. The 'Other items, all as described by MariaDB' list covers vector search, multi-region and deployment/security, and is introduced as a selection, not an exhaustive list. No relative dates (the 'later this month' phrase appears only inside a verbatim quote, next to the explicit November 4, 2026 date). The limits section states what the sources do not establish (full report gated, no third-party repeat, no durable-commit results, 11.8.3-1 setting parity unknown), and each of those statements is true of the five snapshots.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all five committed snapshots under sources/2026-11/mariadb-enterprise-platform-2027-is-generally-available-its-56-throughput-claim-rests-on-a-mariadb-sponsored-test-mariadb-calls-non-durable/ (gunzip then HTML to text; all HTTP 200, no archive fallback, suspicious_patterns null for all five). source-0 (Blocks & Files, Chris Mellor, published 4 Nov 2026): CONFIRMS the same-day coverage, the six-component list, the 30% vector figure, '56 percent higher peak throughput over the last major release in third-party testing' (article correctly quotes 'in third-party testing'), the present-tense 'MariaDB AI Retrieval is available in public preview on MariaDB Cloud', and that it does not mention sponsorship or test conditions. source-1 (press release, 4 Nov 2026, Redwood City and Dublin): CONFIRMS 'generally available today', the six-component list, the Agent Memory/Semantic Cache/AI plugins quotes, 'now delivers up to 30% more queries per second than the last major release', the footnote 1 text (McKnight Consulting Group, 'High-Concurrency TPC-C Benchmarking,' October 2026; 'HammerDB TPROC-C (derived from TPC-C, not an official TPC-C result)'; 'in-memory engine scalability test'; Enterprise Server 12.3.3-0 vs. 11.8.3-1 on Google Cloud; 'Sponsored by MariaDB.'), and 'MariaDB AI Retrieval follows in public preview on MariaDB Cloud later this month.' source-2 (launch blog by Tina Yang, 4 Nov 2026): CONFIRMS 56% more peak throughput than version 11.8 in third-party McKnight testing, 'runs 25% faster than MySQL 9.7.2 at peak performance', the 30% vector figure 'than version 11.8 at the same accuracy', Raft Cluster GA and the 'Writes commit as soon as a majority of nodes confirm...' quote, Exa generally available on premises, BYOC GA running the MariaDB Cloud data plane in AWS, Azure or Google Cloud, FIPS 140-3 through the Enterprise Kubernetes Operator, and 'MariaDB AI Retrieval is available in public preview on MariaDB Cloud.' Minor nuance, not a correction: the blog body gives the 25% MySQL figure with 'It' referring to Enterprise Server 12.3, while its Key takeaways attribute it to the platform; the article follows the Key takeaways. source-3 (engineering blog by Adam Luciano and Steve Shaw, 4 Nov 2026, 'About 4x More OLTP Throughput than 10.6'): CONFIRMS 11.8.3-1 peak 1,702,758 NOPM at 88 virtual users, 12.3.3 2,653,370 NOPM at 152 virtual users, '~1.56x', NOPM defined as New Orders Per Minute, 'The configuration was deliberately in-memory and non-durable.' (in the test-procedure list of the McKnight testbed section, so it describes the same McKnight run that yields the 56%; the sentence is MariaDB's authors' own, and the blog does not say who set the configuration), '12.3.3 ran with innodb_index_shrink = OFF, a non-default setting', c4d-highmem-192-lssd with 96 cores and 192 vCPUs, 768 warehouses, 'McKnight did not test 10.6', the earlier separate run on 'a similar 96-core system', and 'treat the comparisons in this section as indicative rather than like-for-like'. source-4 (report landing page): CONFIRMS 'An independent performance test, sponsored by MariaDB', 56% more at best result vs 11.8, 'about 25% more orders per minute than MySQL 9.7.2 between 64 and 120 users, and 21% more at 152 users', 'At each database's best result, MariaDB's lead was 21%', 'so anyone can repeat the test and check the claims', and that the full report is behind a form. I extracted all 25 quoted strings in the body and matched each against the normalized snapshot text: all 25 are verbatim. Internal link /article/2026-03/20-mariadb-acquires-gridgain-to-build-sub-millisecond-data-infrastructure-for-agentic-ai exists and is described exactly (the March 9 announcement of a definitive agreement to acquire GridGain Systems). Independent-source recount: 1 of 5 (Blocks & Files); 4 are MariaDB first-party. Analysis requirements do not apply (category is News). Allowlist: mariadb.com independently confirmed and added (see findings); blocksandfiles.com already on the list.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabricated or misattributed specifics found. The 56% figure is correctly described as peak-to-peak (11.8.3-1 at 88 users vs 12.3.3 at 152 users), Enterprise Server 12.3.3-0 vs 11.8.3-1, HammerDB TPROC-C. The two MySQL comparisons are presented as MariaDB words them: launch blog '25% faster at peak', report page about 25% at the same load between 64 and 120 users, 21% at 152 users, and 21% at each database's best result. The '4x vs 10.6' figure is correctly described as built on an earlier separate run and, in the blog's own words, indicative rather than like-for-like. The AI Retrieval wording difference (press release 'later this month' vs launch blog and Blocks & Files 'available') is presented with both quotes. Dates (November 4, 2026; October 2026 report) match the sources. The title claim 'Test MariaDB Calls Non-Durable' is accurate: it is MariaDB's engineering blog that says the configuration was deliberately in-memory and non-durable, and the same blog is the source for the 1.56x ratio.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. The title is pointed but attributes the non-durable description to MariaDB, and the body reports it with the vendor's own quotation without characterizing the test as flawed or misleading.
editor_notes.originality: New topic. No prior Herald article on Enterprise Platform 2027, Enterprise Server 12.3 or this benchmark; the only related prior piece is the March GridGain acquisition article, which the article links accurately and which is added as a related article in the meta file.
concerns: Sourcing is overwhelmingly first-party (4 of 5 sources are MariaDB pages) and the one independent source adds no verification; the article is transparent about this and about not having read the gated McKnight report, so no correction is warranted.
Pattern scanner: no suspicious_patterns in any manifest entry, so no false-positive override was needed.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, carefully attributed News coverage of a vendor GA announcement that surfaces the vendor's own disclosure of how its headline benchmark number was produced. Every quote, number, version and date verified against the snapshots; approved without corrections. Featured candidacy: 1 - solid, accurate release coverage with useful benchmark-context for database engineers, but a single vendor's product launch rather than an industry-wide story
